note: Coordinates marked verified:true were cross-checked against the listed source. verified:false means approximate/community-reported — confirm on the live map before relying on them. Never treat unverified data as exact.

destinations.summary_en: A granite hill on the plain of Arafat, about 20 km southeast of Makkah, where pilgrims gather on the Day of Arafah during Hajj. It is in Arafat, not Mina.
destinations.summary_roman: Arafat ke maidan mein ek granite pahari, Makkah se taqreeban 20 km door, jahan Hajj ke din (Yaum-e-Arafah) hujjaj jama hote hain.
destinations.significance: The Prophet ﷺ delivered the Farewell Sermon on the plain of Arafat during his final Hajj. Standing (wuquf) at Arafat is the essential pillar of Hajj.
history_refs: Sahih Muslim – Hadith of the Farewell Pilgrimage
destinations.opening_hours: Open area; accessible year-round outside Hajj restrictions
destinations.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon (cooler hours)
tips: Carry water and sun protection — the plain is exposed.
During Hajj season access is restricted to pilgrims with permits.
destinations.accessibility: Uneven rocky steps to the summit; base viewable from flat ground.

destinations.summary_en: The historic cemetery of Makkah, north of Masjid al-Haram, where Sayyidah Khadijah (RA), the Prophet's ﷺ first wife, and several of his relatives are buried.
destinations.summary_roman: Makkah ka tareekhi qabristan, Masjid al-Haram ke shumal mein, jahan Hazrat Khadijah (RA) aur Nabi ﷺ ke kai rishtedaar madfoon hain.
destinations.significance: Resting place of Sayyidah Khadijah (RA), Abdul Muttalib and Abu Talib. Visited for salam and remembrance of death, per sunnah etiquette of graveyard visits.
destinations.opening_hours: Typically open after Fajr until Isha; women's entry restricted per local rules
tips: Observe graveyard etiquette; photography of graves is discouraged.
Graves are unmarked mounds per local practice.
destinations.accessibility: Flat walking paths at entrance area.
destinations.restrictions: Entry rules enforced at gate; follow posted signage.

destinations.summary_en: A mosque near Jannat al-Mu'alla marking the place where, according to tradition, a group of jinn heard the Prophet ﷺ recite the Qur'an and accepted Islam.
destinations.summary_roman: Jannat al-Mu'alla ke qareeb masjid, jahan riwayat ke mutabiq jinnon ki ek jamaat ne Nabi ﷺ se Quran sun kar Islam qubool kiya.
destinations.significance: Associated with Surah al-Jinn. Also known historically as Masjid al-Bay'ah (of the jinn).
destinations.opening_hours: Open at prayer times
tips: Combine with a visit to Jannat al-Mu'alla next door.

destinations.summary_en: Site west of Makkah (modern Ash-Shumaysi) associated with the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH) and the Pledge of Ridwan. A miqat-area mosque stands near the historic location.
destinations.summary_roman: Makkah ke maghrib mein (Ash-Shumaysi) woh jagah jahan Sulah-e-Hudaybiyyah (6 Hijri) aur Bai'at-e-Ridwan hui.
destinations.significance: The treaty that Allah called 'a clear victory' (Surah al-Fath). Site of Bay'at al-Ridwan under the tree.
history_refs: Surah al-Fath (48); Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Conditions
tips: Both an old ruined mosque and a newer mosque exist in the area.
Coordinates approximate — confirm on map before driving.
destinations.accessibility: Reachable by car on the old Jeddah road.

destinations.summary_en: The 'Mountain of Light' northeast of Masjid al-Haram. Near its summit lies the Cave of Hira, where the Prophet ﷺ received the first revelation (Surah al-Alaq).
destinations.summary_roman: Masjid al-Haram ke shumal-mashriq mein 'Roshni ka Pahar'. Iski choti ke qareeb Ghar-e-Hira hai jahan pehli wahi nazil hui.
destinations.significance: Site of the first revelation: 'Iqra bismi rabbika...' (96:1). A defining moment in Islamic history.
history_refs: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation, Hadith 3
destinations.opening_hours: Open area; Hira Cultural District at the base has its own ticketed hours
destinations.best_time: Pre-dawn or late afternoon; avoid midday heat
tips: The climb takes roughly 1.5–2 hours round trip and is strenuous.
Elderly visitors can view the mountain and visit the Hira Cultural District at the base.
destinations.accessibility: Steep stepped climb; not wheelchair accessible beyond the base.
destinations.restrictions: Climb at your own risk; follow safety signage.

destinations.summary_en: Mountain south of Makkah containing the cave where the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) sheltered for three nights at the start of the Hijrah to Madinah.
destinations.summary_roman: Makkah ke junoob mein pahar jis mein woh ghaar hai jahan Nabi ﷺ aur Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) ne Hijrat ke waqt teen raatein guzarein.
destinations.significance: Mentioned in Surah at-Tawbah (9:40): 'the second of the two, when they were in the cave.'
history_refs: Qur'an 9:40; Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of Abu Bakr
destinations.opening_hours: Open area
tips: The climb is harder and longer than Jabal al-Nour (3–4 hours round trip).
Most visitors view the mountain from the base.
destinations.accessibility: Very steep; base viewable by car.

destinations.summary_en: The nearest point outside the Haram boundary (about 7.5 km from Masjid al-Haram) where residents of Makkah enter ihram for Umrah, named after Aisha (RA) who entered ihram here in 9 AH.
destinations.summary_roman: Haram ki hudood se bahar sab se qareebi jagah jahan Makkah walay Umrah ka ihram bandhte hain; Hazrat Aisha (RA) ne yahan se ihram bandha tha.
destinations.significance: Functions as the miqat for people already inside Makkah intending Umrah.
history_refs: Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim – Aisha's Umrah from Tan'im
destinations.opening_hours: Open through the day; busiest before Umrah times
tips: Ihram garments, showers and shops are available on site.
Taxis routinely run between the Haram and Tan'im.

destinations.summary_en: The two small hills inside Masjid al-Haram between which pilgrims perform Sa'i — seven crossings commemorating Hajar's (AS) search for water for her son Ismail (AS).
destinations.summary_roman: Masjid al-Haram ke andar do choti pahariyan jin ke darmiyan Sa'i ki jati hai — Hazrat Hajra (AS) ki pani ki talash ki yaad mein.
destinations.significance: Named in the Qur'an (2:158): 'Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.' Sa'i is a rite of both Hajj and Umrah.
history_refs: Qur'an 2:158; Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj
destinations.opening_hours: Open 24 hours within Masjid al-Haram
destinations.best_time: Late night / early morning for lighter crowds
tips: The Mas'aa is about 450 m one way (≈3.15 km total for seven laps).
Wheelchair and electric-cart lanes are provided on upper levels.
destinations.restrictions: Within Masjid al-Haram — entry per Haram rules.

destinations.summary_en: The first mosque founded by the Prophet ﷺ upon arriving at Madinah during the Hijrah — widely regarded as the first mosque of Islam.
destinations.summary_roman: Hijrat ke waqt Madinah pohanchte hi Nabi ﷺ ki qaim karda pehli masjid — Islam ki pehli masjid mani jati hai.
destinations.significance: The Prophet ﷺ said that praying two rak'ahs in Quba carries the reward of an Umrah (Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah). Referenced as 'the mosque founded on taqwa' (9:108) per many scholars.
destinations.opening_hours: Open daily; busiest on Saturdays following the sunnah visit
tips: Visiting Quba on Saturday and praying two rak'ahs follows the Prophet's ﷺ practice.
Reachable by the pedestrian Quba Walk from Masjid an-Nabawi (~3.5 km).

destinations.name_en: Masjid al-Qiblatayn (Mosque of the Two Qiblas)
destinations.summary_en: The mosque where, during prayer in 2 AH, the revelation came changing the qibla from Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) to the Kaaba in Makkah.
destinations.summary_roman: Woh masjid jahan namaz ke dauran qibla Bait-ul-Maqdis se Kaaba ki taraf tabdeel hone ki wahi nazil hui.
destinations.significance: Linked to Qur'an 2:144: 'So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram.' Unique for having faced two qiblas in one prayer.
destinations.opening_hours: Open daily around prayer times
tips: The modern rebuilt mosque retains a symbolic second mihrab motif.

destinations.summary_en: The mountain north of Madinah beside which the Battle of Uhud (3 AH) took place. The cemetery of the seventy martyrs, including Sayyiduna Hamza (RA), lies at its foot.
destinations.summary_roman: Madinah ke shumal mein pahar jahan Ghazwa-e-Uhud (3 Hijri) hua. Iske daman mein Shuhada-e-Uhud, bashumool Hazrat Hamza (RA), ka qabristan hai.
destinations.significance: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it' (Bukhari). Site of profound lessons on obedience and sacrifice.
history_refs: Sahih al-Bukhari 4084; Seerah literature on Ghazwat Uhud
destinations.opening_hours: Open area; martyrs' cemetery viewing area open daylight hours
tips: The Archers' Hill (Jabal ar-Rumah) viewing point explains the battle's turning point.
Give salam at the martyrs' enclosure from outside the fence.
destinations.accessibility: Paved viewing areas at the base.
destinations.restrictions: Cemetery enclosure closed to entry; view from perimeter.

destinations.summary_en: The main cemetery of Madinah adjacent to Masjid an-Nabawi, resting place of thousands of Companions and family members of the Prophet ﷺ, including Uthman (RA) and many of the Ahl al-Bayt.
destinations.summary_roman: Masjid-e-Nabawi se mulhiqa Madinah ka markazi qabristan, jahan hazaron Sahaba aur Ahl-e-Bait madfoon hain.
destinations.significance: The Prophet ﷺ regularly visited al-Baqi and prayed for its inhabitants (Sahih Muslim 974).
destinations.opening_hours: Open to men after Fajr and after Asr (times set locally)
tips: Entry windows are limited and may change; check locally.
Maintain graveyard etiquette; graves are unmarked.
destinations.restrictions: Entry windows enforced; women view from outside per local rules.

destinations.summary_en: Marks the place in the valley of Ranuna where the Prophet ﷺ led the first Jumu'ah (Friday) prayer in history, while traveling from Quba into Madinah during the Hijrah.
destinations.summary_roman: Wadi Ranuna mein woh jagah jahan Nabi ﷺ ne Hijrat ke dauran tareekh ka pehla Jumu'ah ada farmaya.
destinations.significance: Site of the first Friday congregational prayer of Islam. This is distinct from the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) sites, which are elsewhere in Madinah.
history_refs: Seerah Ibn Hisham – arrival at Madinah
destinations.opening_hours: Open around prayer times
tips: Located between Quba and the city center — easy to combine with a Quba visit.

destinations.summary_en: The 'Blessed Valley' running along the western side of Madinah, praised in hadith; the miqat of Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) lies on its course.
destinations.summary_roman: Madinah ke maghrib mein behne wali 'Mubarak Wadi' jiska zikr hadith mein aaya hai; Zul-Hulaifa (Abyar Ali) miqat isi par waqe hai.
destinations.significance: The Prophet ﷺ was told in a dream: 'You are in a blessed valley' (Sahih al-Bukhari 1535).
destinations.opening_hours: Open natural area
tips: The valley is long — coordinates point to a central reach; landmarks like Abyar Ali sit along it.
Coordinates approximate for a natural feature.

destinations.summary_en: The town ~150 km southwest of Madinah where the first decisive battle of Islam took place in 2 AH. The cemetery of the fourteen martyrs of Badr is preserved there.
destinations.summary_roman: Madinah se taqreeban 150 km junoob-maghrib mein woh maqam jahan 2 Hijri mein Islam ka pehla faisla-kun maarka hua.
destinations.significance: Called Yawm al-Furqan (the Day of the Criterion) in the Qur'an (8:41). 313 believers prevailed over a far larger force.
destinations.opening_hours: Open area; martyrs' cemetery daylight hours
destinations.best_time: Morning (plan a half-day trip from Madinah)
tips: This is an inter-city drive (~2 hours each way from Madinah) — plan fuel and water.
Not a short local journey from Madinah.
destinations.accessibility: Reachable by highway; flat terrain at site.

destinations.place_query: Wadi al Baida Magnetic Hill Madinah
destinations.summary_en: A valley ~30–40 km northwest of Madinah famous as a 'gravity hill' where vehicles appear to roll uphill — an optical illusion caused by the terrain's slope, popular as a family outing.
destinations.summary_roman: Madinah se 30–40 km shumal-maghrib mein mashhoor wadi jahan gariyan bazahir khud chalti nazar aati hain — zameen ki dhalan ka optical illusion.
destinations.significance: A natural curiosity; popular folklore attributes it to jinn, but the phenomenon is a well-documented gravity-hill illusion. No authentic religious significance.
destinations.opening_hours: Open area
tips: Keep to the paved road; mobile coverage can be weak in parts.
Coordinates approximate — confirm on map before driving.

destinations.summary_en: A cluster of small historic mosques on the western side of Mount Sala' in Madinah, at the site of the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq, 5 AH), including Masjid al-Fath.
destinations.summary_roman: Madinah mein Jabal Sala' ke maghribi hisse par choti tareekhi masajid ka majmua, Ghazwa-e-Khandaq (5 Hijri) ke maqam par.
destinations.significance: Associated with the Battle of the Trench where the Prophet ﷺ made the famous supplication at Masjid al-Fath. This Khandaq site is in Madinah and distinct from Masjid al-Jumu'ah.
history_refs: Seerah on Ghazwat al-Khandaq; Surah al-Ahzab (33)
destinations.opening_hours: Exterior area open; interiors vary
tips: Today several of the original seven are preserved near the large modern Khandaq mosque.
destinations.accessibility: Short walks on paved and stepped paths.

destinations.summary_en: A historic well in the Quba area from which the Prophet ﷺ drank; narrations state he instructed that water from Ghars be used to wash his body after his passing.
destinations.summary_roman: Quba ke ilaqe mein tareekhi kunwan jis se Nabi ﷺ ne pani piya; riwayat ke mutabiq aap ﷺ ke ghusl ke liye isi ka pani istemal hua.
destinations.significance: One of the historic wells of Madinah tied to the Prophet's ﷺ daily life; recently restored as a heritage site.
history_refs: Sunan Ibn Majah 1468 (graded variously); Madinah heritage records
destinations.opening_hours: Viewable heritage site; hours set locally
tips: A short drive from Masjid Quba.

destinations.summary_en: The tallest fountain of its kind in the world, jetting Red Sea water over 260 m into the air off Jeddah's corniche. Illuminated at night.
destinations.summary_roman: Dunya ka sab se buland fountain jo Bahr-e-Ahmar ka pani 260 meter se oopar uchalta hai; raat ko roshan hota hai.
destinations.significance: An iconic modern landmark of Jeddah, donated by King Fahd; operating since 1985.
destinations.opening_hours: Visible from the corniche; typically runs afternoon to late night
tips: Best photo spots are along the Jeddah Corniche walkway.
destinations.accessibility: Corniche promenade is flat and accessible.
destinations.restrictions: Viewed from shore — the fountain itself is offshore.

destinations.summary_en: Jeddah's public aquarium on the corniche with 200+ marine species from the Red Sea and beyond, plus dolphin and sea-lion shows — a favourite family stop.
destinations.summary_roman: Jeddah corniche par aquarium jisme 200+ samundari species aur dolphin shows hain — families ke liye behtareen.
destinations.significance: The first public aquarium in Saudi Arabia.
destinations.opening_hours: Daily; check official site for current timings
tips: Tickets and show times are published on the official website — prices not hardcoded here; verify before visiting.

destinations.summary_en: A white-domed mosque built on stilts over the Red Sea on Jeddah's corniche; at high tide it appears to float on the water.
destinations.summary_roman: Bahr-e-Ahmar par banayi gayi safed gumbad wali masjid jo high tide par pani par tairti nazar aati hai.
destinations.significance: Built in 1985; blends modern and traditional Islamic architecture and is a celebrated photography spot.
destinations.opening_hours: Open daily; non-prayer visiting hours vary
tips: Dress modestly; visitors are welcome outside prayer times.

destinations.place_query: Al Tayebat International City Museum Jeddah
destinations.summary_en: A sprawling museum complex in traditional Hijazi architecture with hundreds of rooms covering Islamic heritage, pre-Islamic Arabia, Saudi history, calligraphy and Jeddah's old-city craftsmanship.
destinations.summary_roman: Hijazi tarz ki azeem imarat mein museum jisme Islami virsa, Saudi tareekh aur khattati ke sainkron rooms hain.
destinations.significance: One of the Kingdom's richest private heritage collections.
destinations.opening_hours: Sat–Thu, morning and evening sessions (verify locally)
tips: Coordinates approximate — confirm on map before driving.
Ticket prices change; check at entrance rather than relying on old listings.

destinations.name_en: The National Museum of Saudi Arabia
destinations.place_query: National Museum of Saudi Arabia Riyadh
destinations.summary_en: The Kingdom's flagship museum in the King Abdulaziz Historical Center, with eight galleries spanning Arabian history from prehistory through the Prophet's ﷺ mission to the modern Saudi state.
destinations.summary_roman: King Abdulaziz Historical Center mein Saudi Arab ka markazi museum — qadeem Arab se le kar daur-e-Nabawi ﷺ aur jadeed riyasat tak 8 galleries.
destinations.significance: Includes dedicated galleries on the Prophet's ﷺ mission and the Hajj routes.
destinations.opening_hours: Closed Sundays typically; verify current schedule on official channels
tips: Combine with Murabba Palace in the same historical center.

destinations.summary_en: The historic mud-brick city on Wadi Hanifah, birthplace of the first Saudi state (1727), now restored with the Bujairi Terrace dining district beside the At-Turaif ruins.
destinations.summary_roman: Wadi Hanifah par qadeem mitti ki eenton ka shehar — pehli Saudi riyasat ki janam bhoomi, ab Bujairi Terrace ke sath bahal shuda.
destinations.significance: Cradle of the Saudi state and a centre of Najdi architecture and heritage.
destinations.opening_hours: District open daily; attraction hours vary
tips: Book At-Turaif entry online in peak season.
destinations.accessibility: Pedestrianized zones; some uneven heritage paths.

destinations.place_query: Edge of the World Jebel Fihrayn
destinations.summary_en: Dramatic cliffs on the Tuwaiq escarpment ~100 km northwest of Riyadh, offering a sheer drop and uninterrupted horizon views over an ancient sea bed.
destinations.summary_roman: Riyadh se ~100 km door Tuwaiq ki chattanein jahan se be-intiha ufaq ka manzar milta hai.
destinations.significance: A signature natural wonder of central Arabia along old caravan routes.
destinations.opening_hours: Open area; access road conditions vary — often closed in rain
tips: A 4x4 vehicle and an experienced driver/guide are strongly recommended; the last stretch is off-road.
No facilities on site — carry water, fuel and offline maps.
Coordinates approximate for a natural area — follow a guided route.
destinations.accessibility: Rugged terrain; not accessible for limited mobility.
destinations.restrictions: Access occasionally restricted by authorities; check before travel.

destinations.summary_en: The clay-and-mudbrick fort in old Riyadh whose 1902 capture by King Abdulaziz began the unification of modern Saudi Arabia; now a museum of that story.
destinations.summary_roman: Purane Riyadh ka mitti ka qila jiski 1902 mein fatah se jadeed Saudi Arab ke ittehad ka aghaz hua; ab museum hai.
destinations.significance: Site of the famous 1902 raid; the spearhead lodged in its door is still shown.
destinations.opening_hours: Open most days; verify session times locally
destinations.best_time: Morning, then explore adjacent Souq Al Zal
tips: Free entry historically; confirm at gate.

destinations.summary_en: Riyadh's flagship entertainment district of fountains, dining, shows and themed zones, anchored around the Riyadh Season calendar.
destinations.summary_roman: Riyadh ka sab se bara entertainment district — fountains, khanay, shows aur themed zones.
destinations.significance: Centerpiece of the Riyadh Season entertainment program.
destinations.opening_hours: Seasonal; evening-focused — check official Riyadh Season channels
tips: Operates seasonally; zones, tickets and hours change each season — verify before planning.
Family-friendly but very crowded on weekends.
destinations.restrictions: Seasonal opening — may be closed off-season.

destinations.summary_en: UNESCO World Heritage district of Diriyah — the mud-brick seat of the first Saudi state with Salwa Palace and restored Najdi architecture.
destinations.summary_roman: Diriyah ka UNESCO World Heritage district — pehli Saudi riyasat ka markaz, Salwa Palace ke sath.
destinations.significance: Inscribed by UNESCO in 2010 as an outstanding example of Najdi architecture and the historic capital of the Saudi dynasty.
destinations.opening_hours: Ticketed entry; hours vary by season
tips: Book tickets via official Diriyah platforms in busy seasons.
destinations.accessibility: Partially accessible; heritage lanes are uneven in places.

destinations.name_en: Taif — Mountain City, Sarawat & Masjid Abdullah ibn Abbas
destinations.summary_en: The cool mountain city of the Sarawat range (≈1,800 m), famed for roses and fruit orchards. Home to Masjid Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) and linked to the Prophet's ﷺ difficult journey to Taif; local tradition in the Al-Mathnah orchards remembers the meeting with Addas.
destinations.summary_roman: Sarawat ke pahadon ka thanda shehar (≈1800m), gulab aur baghon ke liye mashhoor. Masjid Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) yahan hai; Nabi ﷺ ke Safar-e-Taif aur Addas ki mulaqat se nisbat.
destinations.significance: Scene of the Prophet's ﷺ patient endurance in the 10th year of prophethood and his supplication of hope; later embraced Islam after Hunayn.
history_refs: Seerah Ibn Hisham – the journey to Ta'if
destinations.opening_hours: City — always open; attractions vary
destinations.best_time: Spring (rose season) and summer evenings; Al Hada cable car at sunset
tips: The exact historic orchard site linked with Addas (Al-Mathnah area) is traditional and its precise spot is unverified — visit respectfully without assuming exact locations.
Drive up via the scenic Al Hada mountain road.
destinations.accessibility: City fully accessible; mountain viewpoints vary.

destinations.name_en: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra)
destinations.name_ar: مركز الملك عبدالعزيز الثقافي العالمي – إثراء
destinations.summary_en: Aramco's iconic pebble-shaped cultural landmark in Dhahran — museum galleries, a grand library, cinema, children's museum and the Energy Exhibit.
destinations.summary_roman: Dhahran mein Aramco ka mashhoor cultural center — museums, azeem library, cinema aur Energy Exhibit.
destinations.significance: Opened 2017 at the site of Saudi Arabia's first commercial oil well discovery area; a national symbol of knowledge and creativity.
destinations.opening_hours: Open daily except some Mondays; check official site
tips: General entry to many areas is free; special exhibits ticketed — verify on the official site.

destinations.summary_en: A man-made leisure island off the Dammam Corniche connected by a causeway — green lawns, palm-lined walkways, play areas and Gulf views, popular for family evenings.
destinations.summary_roman: Dammam Corniche se mulhiqa masnoi jazeera — sarsabz lawns, walkways aur Gulf ke nazare; families ki pasandeeda jagah.
destinations.significance: A landmark of the Dammam waterfront since the 1980s corniche development.
destinations.opening_hours: Open daily
tips: Coordinates approximate — confirm on map before driving.
Good picnic spot; weekends are busy.
destinations.accessibility: Flat paths across the causeway and island.
